title: ByRef versus ByVal: caller variable and local parameter
requirements: Use an Integer-valued teaching example with caller variable x=7. Left panel ByRef: changing the parameter to 9 changes x. Right panel ByVal: the local parameter becomes 9 while x remains 7.
Do not draw a complete copied Deck or Hand array for ByVal. The supplied code mixes structures and array references; source-file semantics alone do not substantiate deep-copy claims.
Explicitly label the example Integer values. An array-reference extension requires the R04a evidence decision and its own explanatory state.
Historical default-passing statements stay out of the graphic until separately verified.
beats: 0–1.5 s: three columns show the code; x holds 5 everywhere.
1.5–3 s: the call line Bump(x) / bump(x) is the running line.
3–4.5 s: entering the Sub: ByVal shows n as a copy of 5 beside x; ByRef shows n as a tag whose arrow points back at x.
4.5–6 s: n = n + 1 runs: the ByVal copy becomes 6 while x stays 5; under ByRef x itself becomes 6.
6–7.5 s: End Sub: the ByVal copy is struck through and marked discarded; the ByRef tag fades.
7.5–10 s: held result: x is still 5 (ByVal) against x is now 6 (ByRef).
checks: The two results are numerically unambiguous: x stays 5 under ByVal, x becomes 6 under ByRef.
No duplicated array storage is depicted as an automatic result of ByVal.
ByRef and ByVal labels remain visible in every state.

revision_2.change: Diagram replaced by a code-driven demonstration: Sub Bump(ByVal n As Integer) / Sub Bump(ByRef n As Integer), n = n + 1, called with x = 5; ByVal leaves x at 5, ByRef makes it 6; third column C++ void bump(int n) / void bump(int& n). Variants byval, byref, cpp. About 10 s of motion with a held end state.
